name: FR13A rice selection from Dhalputtia, Cuttack
description: Rice researchers at Cuttack selected FR13A from Dhalputtia, a rice landrace grown by farmers in what is now Odisha. FR13A became a source of temporary complete-submergence tolerance for subsequent breeding.

date.label: by the 1950s
date.basis: The FAO case study retrospectively places an FR13A release in the early 1950s. The 1950s is used as a broad upper bound for the selection's existence.

events.statement: FR13A existed as a flood-tolerant selection derived from Dhalputtia at Cuttack.

evidence.locator: p. 64, “Discovery of flood tolerance in rice and attempts to develop tolerant varieties”
evidence.supports: The authors identify FR13A as a selection from Dhalaputia and attribute release to Cuttack.

evidence.locator: Passport data, “Acquisition Date”, “Provenance of material”, “Ancestral information (pedigree)” and “Accession name”
evidence.supports: The accession passport confirms Indian provenance and Dhalputtia ancestry.

evidence.locator: Section “Tolerance and susceptibility to submergence”, paragraph identifying the source of FR13A
evidence.supports: Corroborates the selection and ancestry, while differing on the period of release.

date.label: 1 October 2006
date.basis: Date recorded for this accession in the genebank passport.

events.statement: The International Rice Genebank passport records the acquisition of FR 13 A accession IRGC 117267.

evidence.locator: Passport data, “Acquisition Date”, “Provenance of material”, “Ancestral information (pedigree)” and “Accession name”
evidence.supports: The date belongs to this accession and does not date the original transfer of FR13A to IRRI.

earliest_record.rationale: The retrospective accounts support the selection's existence by the 1950s. Its exact selection and release dates remain open.

unresolved.note: Find contemporary Cuttack station documentation and release papers. The early-1950s retrospective release account and a published 1940s account give different dates.
The farming history of Dhalputtia before selection and the route and date of the original material reaching IRRI remain unverified.
